Hi Alex —

Appreciate the clarity. I've drafted two tidy options you can share with procurement/legal; attaching a short one-pager (POC_Amendment_Options.pdf) that summarizes both. High-level:

Option A — Ops hour-bank (recommended for integration-heavy work):
- 40 engineering/ops hours (shadowing + hands-on debugging) valid during the 3-week extension
- Priority paging during business hours, 4-hour response objective for P1s, 8-hour for P2s
- No change to token billing; hours are consumed for assistance only
- Price: $9,500 (discounted rate, one-time)

Option B — Monetary credit + standard SLAs (recommended if you prefer straight billing):
- $12,000 one-time credit applied against hosted usage during the extension window
- Includes enhanced monitoring dashboard access and a shared on-call rotation for the 3 weeks
- We can include a 99.5% availability target for the POC endpoint and a 6-hour response SLA for P1s

If procurement wants an SLA tighter than 4 hours that's doable but requires a small additional premium (we've modeled $2,000 extra for guaranteed 3-hour response). Both options are compatible with the current contract; we can sign a short amendment or an addendum.

Next steps if either looks good: I can produce a one-click DocuSign amendment and loop legal for a final redline.
